summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and prior liver transplant presented with acute fever, rigors, and right upper quadrant pain. Initial labs showed elevated liver enzymes, raising concern for infection or transplant rejection. Imaging revealed patent hepatic vasculature without biliary dilation, and blood cultures were negative. She was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics for 36 hours, after which her symptoms rapidly improved and liver function tests began to normalize. Given her clinical improvement, antibiotics were discontinued and a liver biopsy was avoided. The episode was attributed to a likely transient biliary obstruction, possibly from a passed stone. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her transplant team and complete outpatient lab monitoring.
